title: Data Collection for Basic Research on Drone-Based Contactless Multi-Person Vital Sign Assessment Using an Image Processing Algorithm
summary:
In major incidents, such as severe accidents or other events involving large numbers of casualties, personnel and technical resources are often limited. As a result, vital signs such as heart rate and respiratory activity cannot always be monitored continuously in all patients. Consequently, changes in a patient's clinical condition may be detected with delay.

In addition, conventional contact-based monitoring methods present further challenges in such scenarios, as they require the availability of appropriate medical devices and are both time- and personnel-intensive. Therefore, comprehensive and continuous monitoring of all affected patients is often not feasible under these conditions.

Contactless vital sign monitoring may therefore provide a future opportunity to improve patient monitoring even under challenging operational conditions. One promising approach is the assessment of vital signs using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs, drones). The VitalKITE research project builds upon previous findings and is developing a demonstrator capable of continuously monitoring patients' vital signs from the air.

The aim of the present study is to evaluate the performance of the algorithm for drone-based aerial vital sign assessment and to investigate the influence of different environmental and physiological conditions on measurement accuracy. To enable an appropriate evaluation of the collected data, repeated comparisons with contact-based reference measurements are required. These reference measurements will be acquired simultaneously with the video recordings using certified medical devices.
